stem: RA 11898, the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Act of 2022, added new rules to RA 9003. Which businesses are obliged to carry out EPR for plastic packaging?
choices: Large enterprises generating plastic packaging waste
All businesses selling goods in plastic, big or small
Micro, small and medium enterprises only
Only the junk shops and recyclers buying plastic waste
answer: Large enterprises generating plastic packaging waste
hints: EPR makes producers responsible for their product even after it is used and thrown away. The law does not cover every business.
Look at the new Section 44-B of RA 9003, added by RA 11898. It names the obliged enterprises by size.
Section 44-B says one group "shall not be covered" but is encouraged to join voluntarily. Remove the choices that go against this, then check what is left.

solution.methodName: Name who is responsible, then check the exact role

steps.action: Recall the definition of EPR in Section 3(m-1), added by RA 11898: it requires "producers to be environmentally responsible throughout the life cycle of a product, especially its post-consumer or end-of-life stage."
steps.why: Post-consumer means after the buyer has used it. So the producer must help recover its plastic waste.

steps.action: Read Section 44-B: the obliged enterprises are "large enterprises that generate plastic packaging waste."
Note the exclusion: micro, small and medium enterprises "shall not be covered," though they are encouraged to practice EPR voluntarily.
The answer is large enterprises generating plastic packaging waste.

trapNotes.All businesses selling goods in plastic,: Size matters. Section 44-B says micro, small and medium enterprises are not covered.
trapNotes.Micro, small and medium enterprises only: This is the reverse of the rule. These smaller businesses are not covered; they may join only voluntarily.
trapNotes.Only the junk shops and recyclers buying: EPR falls on product producers, such as brand owners, manufacturers and importers (Section 3(w-2)), not on buyers of scrap.

sourceRef.citation: RA 9003, Sections 3(m-1), 3(w-2) and 44-B, as added by RA 11898 (Extended Producer Responsibility Act of 2022)
